storyObjective.viewer: First-time salaried filers preparing to file taxes for the first time.
storyObjective.viewerProblem: They don't understand why their W-2 numbers don't match their expected pay, or how confident to be about when a refund will arrive.
storyObjective.centralPromise: By the end of this video, you'll be able to read your own W-2 Box 1 with confidence.
storyObjective.transformationPayoff: From confused about unfamiliar form numbers to able to verify their own paycheck math.
storyObjective.emotionalDirection: From mild anxiety about an unfamiliar form to calm, grounded confidence.
storyObjective.editorialAngle: Arithmetic-first explanation grounded in the IRS's own guidance, not generic tax advice.
storyObjective.expectedTakeaway: Box 1 excludes specific pre-tax deductions, and refund timing this season carries real uncertainty worth planning around.

hook.curiosityMechanism: Most viewers assume their W-2 gross pay is what gets taxed — Box 1 quietly says otherwise.
hook.viewerQuestion: Why is the number in Box 1 smaller than what you actually earned?
hook.payoffExpectation: Viewers will understand exactly which deductions shrink Box 1 and be able to check their own form.

beats.purpose: Open with the counterintuitive gap between gross pay and Box 1 to create immediate curiosity.
beats.viewerQuestion: Why is Box 1 smaller than what you actually earned?
beats.expectedViewerState: Curious and slightly unsettled about a number they assumed they understood.
beats.transitionIntent: Move from the surprising gap into why understanding W-2 boxes matters before filing.

beats.purpose: Establish why a first-time filer needs to understand their own W-2 before trusting any number on it.
beats.expectedViewerState: Motivated to keep watching because the stakes (accurate filing, avoiding surprises) feel personal.
beats.transitionIntent: Move from motivation into the specific mechanism behind Box 1.

beats.purpose: Explain exactly what Box 1 excludes and why, using the IRS's own stated mechanism.
beats.expectedViewerState: Understands that Box 1 is federal taxable wages, not gross pay, and knows the specific deductions responsible.
beats.transitionIntent: Narrow from the general mechanism to the specific limits of what it covers.

beats.purpose: Clarify that the exclusion applies to specific deduction types, not every pre-tax benefit, to avoid overgeneralizing.
beats.expectedViewerState: Understands the mechanism's actual scope rather than assuming it covers every kind of benefit.
requiredConcepts: not every pre-tax benefit is covered
beats.transitionIntent: Shift from the mechanics of Box 1 to the open question of refund timing.
beats.qualification: Supplied evidence names only two specific deduction types (401(k) contributions, cafeteria plan benefits); do not claim the exclusion covers every pre-tax benefit.

beats.purpose: Raise the question of how long a refund actually takes this season, using the IRS's own stated estimate.
beats.viewerQuestion: How long will my refund really take?
beats.expectedViewerState: Aware of the official 21-day estimate and anticipating whether it actually holds.
beats.transitionIntent: Move from the official estimate into the reports that complicate it.

beats.purpose: Present the conflicting reports of longer refund waits this season without resolving which figure is correct.
beats.expectedViewerState: Holds both the official estimate and the anecdotal delay reports at once, without a false sense of certainty either way.
beats.transitionIntent: Move from open uncertainty into the practical payoff of the video.
beats.qualification: The 21-day estimate is officially stated but some filers report much longer waits this season; present both without asserting either is definitively accurate for every filer.

beats.purpose: Deliver the practical payoff: viewers can now read their own W-2 Box 1 with confidence.
beats.expectedViewerState: Confident they can check their own form and set realistic refund expectations.
requiredConcepts: applying the Box 1 mechanism to their own form
beats.transitionIntent: Close the loop back to the opening question before the call to action.

beats.purpose: Prompt the viewer to subscribe for the upcoming refund-tracking follow-up video.
beats.expectedViewerState: Motivated to follow for the next practical step.

data.pacingStrategy: Open fast to hook attention, slow into the explanation and the unresolved refund conflict where the viewer needs time to absorb nuance, then close at a brisk pace for the payoff and CTA.

payoff.description: Viewers leave able to read their own W-2 Box 1 confidently and understand why refund timing carries real uncertainty this season.
payoff.qualification: The refund-timing figure remains contested this season (CLAIM_REFUND_21_DAYS is CONFLICTING); the payoff must present it as the IRS's typical guidance, not a guaranteed outcome.

conclusion.summaryApproach: Recap the Box 1 mechanism briefly and reinforce cautious, well-informed expectations around refund timing.
conclusion.finalTakeaway: Understanding your W-2 boxes turns filing from confusing to controllable.

ctaStrategy.rationale: Viewers interested in W-2 literacy are a strong match for a follow-up video on tracking their actual refund status.

researchGaps.description: No verified claim addresses whether the IRS refund timeline changed from prior seasons; CLAIM_TIMELINE_CHANGE is UNSUPPORTED, so this angle could not be included.
researchGaps.impactOnStory: The video cannot address year-over-year timeline changes without additional research.

researchGaps.description: The Box 12 code D definition claim is marked DO_NOT_USE by Agent 03 due to insufficient primary sourcing, so it was excluded from the story entirely.
researchGaps.impactOnStory: The video omits any Box 12 code explanation; could be added once a primary IRS source is verified.

data.readinessRationale: Sufficient SAFE_TO_USE and properly-qualified USE_WITH_QUALIFICATION claims support a coherent, honestly-caveated narrative; duration is within tolerance and no critical (HIGH-severity) research gaps block scripting.

assumptions.statement: Assumed the primary viewer is a first-time filer based on topicOpportunity's angle, since no explicit audience persona was supplied.

limitations: Only eight verified claims were supplied, four of which are DO_NOT_USE; the narrative leans heavily on two SAFE_TO_USE claims.
The refund-timeline conflict could not be resolved and required a qualification-preserving beat rather than a definitive answer.
